title.narrative: Integrated services to crisis affected communities in Abergele, Tsagibiji, Ziquala and Habru Woredas in the Amhara region

description.narrative: ltpgtPAD is proposing an integrated emergency response project in Ziquala, Abergele, Tsagibiji, and Habru woredas of the Waghimira and North Wollo zones in Amhara Region, to support crisis affected IDPs, affected host communities and recently returned vulnerable persons. The proposed project aims to provide immediate lifesaving humanitarian support to those who are in need. ltbrgtThe focus areas include MPCA, ESNFI, as well as Nutrition. PAD plans to implement this project in collaboration with Action for Sustainable Development and Environmental Protection Organization (ASDEPO) as co-implementing partner. ASDEPO brings expertise in Nutrition and an active national nutrition cluster member with an extensive experience in different parts of the country. UNOCHA's report (OCHA, November, 2023) highlights the need for immediate intervention in all sectors in Waghimira zone mainly for affected vulnerable groups such as women and children. The multidimensional crises, including armed conflict, displacement, and drought have increased the risks faced by these groups. The affected communities’ resort to negative coping mechanisms such as child marriage, family separation, child labor and migration due to challenges in meeting basic needs. Safety concerns in the target woreda increasingly improved as compared with the previous three months. This allows PAD and ASDEPO to intervene and execute planned activities within the stated time-frame. ltbrgtTo address the urgent nutrition related crisis, ASDEPO will implement activities to respond to the needs of children, pregnant and lactating mothers in Ziquala and Tsagibiji woredas. ltbrgtWhereas, PAD will execute ESNFI and MPCA sectors activities to the prevailing needs in Ziquala and Abergele woredas. Using the three sectors, MPCA, Nutrition and ESNFI, PAD and ASDEPO will address a total of 17,601 (F=11,381) crisis affected individuals with a total budget of $800,000 USD. Of which, 531 (F=360) are persons with disabilities and close to 65% of the total beneficiaries are females. ltbrgtThe proposed activities and budget allocation are based on the needs identified in three woredas following the multisectoral assessment conducted by ASDEPO and PAD as well as OCHA. The project aims to integrate immediate lifesaving response activities with durable solutions that contribute to the recovery and resilience of the target populations. Cross-cutting areas such as gender equality, protection, and accountability are mainstreamed throughout the proposed project activities. Proper monitoring and evaluation will be conducted by PAD and ASDEPO to inform program management decisions based on evidence from the field. Joint monitoring sessions will also be conducted periodically with government counterparts. PAD and ASDEPO actively participate in the cluster system at both national and sub-national levels. Efforts will be made to strengthen coordination and reporting of project activities to the donor and clusters via Activity Info. ltbrgtlt/pgt
